aria: Animated recap of the Mavericks' 110 to 100 home win over the Clippers: Kyrie Irving's 26-foot pull-up three in transition with 3:30 left that made it 100 to 88 during an 11 to 0 run, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Irving's 25 points with 12 in the fourth quarter, the top scorers, how Dallas won, and Sunday's game at Utah.

notes: Box score from the Mavericks' 110–100 home win over the LA Clippers on Nov 21, 2026, from the Covers box score, checked against the Associated Press, the Dallas Sports Journal and 95.3 The Score. The player lines add up to both team totals (110 and 100). The quarter scores (23–29–26–32 to 26–18–30–26) add up to both totals: Dallas led 52–44 at the half and 78–74 after three (Dallas Sports Journal; 95.3 The Score). Fast-break points (22–12), points in the paint (40–32), steals (10–6), blocks (3–7), threes made (13–15) and both biggest leads (Dallas 15, Los Angeles 9) are from the Covers box score; points off turnovers (22–13) are from 95.3 The Score, and the 22 also from the Dallas Sports Journal. The AP's lede gives Cooper Flagg 8 rebounds and 6 assists; the box score and 95.3 The Score give 6 rebounds and 8 assists, which is used here. The AP has the Clippers winning the boards 54–52 (team rebounds included); the player lines total 53 each, so rebounds are left out. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Saturday's games.

Dallas won its fifth straight home game (Dallas Sports Journal); the Clippers lost their third straight and are 0–7 on the road (AP). Kris Dunn's corner three with 5:12 left cut it to 91–88, then Dallas scored the next 11 points in 69 seconds: Daniel Gafford's hook at 4:18 (93–88), Max Christie's breakaway layup after a steal at 4:01 (95–88), Zaccharie Risacher's breakaway dunk after a steal at 3:42, Kyrie Irving's 26-foot pull-up three at 3:30 (100–88) and Risacher's dunk at 3:09 (102–88) (Dallas Sports Journal; AP: "the Mavericks scored 11 in a row aided by two Los Angeles turnovers"). Christie, Risacher and Gafford had steals in a 32-second span of the run (Dallas Sports Journal). Irving opened 1 of 7 and scored 12 in the fourth quarter (AP). P.J. Washington missed the game with an illness (AP; Dallas Sports Journal). Dallas plays at Utah on Sunday, Nov 22 at 7:00 PM ET (6:00 PM CT, Yahoo/Roundtable Sports; site schedule).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Kyrie Irving's 26-foot pull-up three in transition at 3:30 of the fourth quarter (Dallas Sports Journal: "Gafford took the ball from Lopez at 3:33 to start a break that Irving finished with a 26-foot pull-up 3 at 3:30 for a 100-88 lead"). The board's 97–88 before the shot follows from the three. No source says which side of the floor the shot came from; the template draws a pull-up three in front of the defender, and the steal is not animated. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Dallas Mavericks or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The player in the play of the game is drawn to Kyrie Irving's listed 6-foot-2 and 195 pounds with No. 11 (Basketball-Reference; Wikipedia), with his arms scaled to a 6-foot-4 wingspan measured at the 2011 draft combine (Tankathon). He is drawn in Dallas's home white with the default figure look (no approved look yet). It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
